narrativeReportMd:
# MedicinalProductInteraction R4→R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`MedicinalProductInteraction` has high-impact breaking changes. The R4 resource is not present as a same-name R6 resource; interaction content is represented by the broader `ClinicalUseDefinition` resource with `type = "interaction"` and an `interaction` backbone.

## Scope
I analyzed the R4 StructureDefinition and the R6 package artifacts that identify the likely replacement, principally `ClinicalUseDefinition`. Inherited `Resource`/`DomainResource` changes are out of scope.

## Main migration themes
Migration is a structural transform: change `resourceType`, add the required root discriminator, move interaction fields under `ClinicalUseDefinition.interaction`, update subject/interactant targets, wrap coded effects into CodeableReference, and preserve old free text/context through extensions or narrative where no base element exists.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact issues are resource identity removal/merge, mandatory and retyped `subject`, the required discriminator and branch invariants, changed interactant targets, and `effect` changing to CodeableReference.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is important for confirming official mapping, preserving R4 `description`, converting product/substance references, and choosing downgrade policies for R6-only context fields and repeated management actions.

## Backward-compatible design observations
The consolidation into `ClinicalUseDefinition` is probably justified, but migration could have been eased with an official ConceptMap/StructureMap, deprecated compatibility resource/profile, or an optional interaction-level description.

## Follow-up analysis
Follow-up should cover full `ClinicalUseDefinition`, the old/new medicinal-product and substance resource families, base `Resource`/`DomainResource` inherited changes, and terminology expansions for R6 interaction value sets.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: R6 removes the standalone `MedicinalProductInteraction` resource and folds interaction content into `ClinicalUseDefinition.type = "interaction"`. The main migration risks are resource identity/API breakage, mandatory and retyped `subject`, moved branch-specific fields with changed reference targets, and R6-only context that cannot be downgraded to R4. Confidence is high for computable StructureDefinition changes but lower for official rationale because no local cross-version map was available.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Treat the migration as a structural transform: change resource identity, add the root discriminator, nest interaction details, update product/substance references, wrap CodeableConcept effects into CodeableReference, and preserve text/context fields through extensions or narrative when no base element exists.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the same-name R6 resource is absent and that `ClinicalUseDefinition.interaction` is the practical counterpart, based on the R6 StructureDefinition, package index, `fhir-old-types`, and interaction search parameter. Confidence would improve with official migration maps, narrative release notes, and terminology expansions.

findings.title: MedicinalProductInteraction resource is absent in R6 and interaction content is merged into ClinicalUseDefinition

oldState.summary: R4 defines a concrete resource type `MedicinalProductInteraction`.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 instances use `resourceType: "MedicinalProductInteraction"` and validate against the same-name resource StructureDefinition.

newState.summary: R6 has no same-name StructureDefinition; the comparable model is `ClinicalUseDefinition` with `type = "interaction"` and an `interaction` backbone.

semanticText.short: A single issue - either an indication, contraindication, interaction or an undesirable effect for a medicinal product, medication, device or procedure

newState.narrativeMd: The R6 package contains `ClinicalUseDefinition`, an `interaction` branch, and a `fhir-old-types` entry for `MedicinalProductInteraction`, indicating the old resource name is no longer used.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `ClinicalUseDefinition.interaction`, the R6 interaction search parameter, and the `fhir-old-types` listing make `ClinicalUseDefinition` the likely replacement. It is a merge/consolidation, not a simple rename.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A conformant R6 parser or validator will not accept `resourceType: "MedicinalProductInteraction"`. Client SDKs, REST routes, generated classes, canonical profile references, and dispatch logic that name the R4 resource must be changed. In reverse, only R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition` resources with `type = "interaction"` are candidates for R4 downgrade.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Clinical decision support or regulated product-label systems could omit interaction knowledge if the resource-type migration is missed.

justification.inferredGoal: Consolidate medicinal-product clinical-use concepts into one resource with a type discriminator.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain a deprecated R6 compatibility resource alongside ClinicalUseDefinition for a transition period.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal, consolidating related clinical-use concepts under `ClinicalUseDefinition`, is coherent and supported by the R6 type discriminator and interaction branch. The break is large, but avoiding it entirely would require keeping the old resource identity in the base package, which would materially undermine consolidation and force servers, clients, search, profiles, and examples to support two representations of the same interaction knowledge.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have kept `MedicinalProductInteraction` as a deprecated compatibility resource, possibly constrained to map to `ClinicalUseDefinition.type = "interaction"`. That would preserve most R4 instances and APIs during transition, but it is only a partial alternative because it duplicates a whole resource model; deprecated resource types can persist indefinitely, fragment interoperability, and accumulate parallel guidance. StructureMap or conversion guidance would help migration but is not itself a backward-compatible base R6 design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves legacy wire identity but creates duplicate resource representations and long-lived support burden.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `id`, `name`, and `type` as `MedicinalProductInteraction`.
R6 defines `ClinicalUseDefinition` as the local resource carrying interaction details.
R6 `fhir-old-types` includes `MedicinalProductInteraction` as an old resource name no longer used.
R6 has an interaction-specific search parameter on `ClinicalUseDefinition.interaction.type`.

examples.examplesMd: The first fragment fails R6 resource-type recognition. The second shows the replacement identity pattern; full migration must also move interaction-specific fields under `interaction`.

findings.narrativeMd: The top-level resource identity changed. R4 had a standalone `MedicinalProductInteraction`; R6 models interactions as one branch of the broader `ClinicalUseDefinition` resource. This breaks direct instance validation and most generated/runtime APIs.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances are old-valid/new-invalid without transformation. R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition` instances can be downgraded to R4 only when the root discriminator says they are interactions; indications, contraindications, undesirable effects, and warnings are outside the R4 target resource's domain.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Migrate storage, REST endpoints, resource dispatch, profiles, and model classes from `MedicinalProductInteraction` to `ClinicalUseDefinition`. Set `type` to `interaction` and put interaction-specific content under `ClinicalUseDefinition.interaction`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The merge is understandable, but an official compatibility profile or mapping artifact would have reduced migration risk. Without it, implementers must infer mappings from the StructureDefinitions.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The replacement identity is inferred from local computable artifacts because no official cross-version map was present.

findings.title: R6 requires a root type discriminator and gates the interaction branch with invariants

oldState.summary: The R4 resource type itself implied an interaction; no separate mandatory discriminator existed.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 did have `MedicinalProductInteraction.type`, but that meant the kind of interaction, such as drug-drug or drug-food, not the root clinical-use issue type.

newState.summary: R6 `ClinicalUseDefinition.type` is `1..1 code` with required binding; `interaction` content is valid only when type is `interaction`.
newState.narrativeMd: A migrated interaction must carry primitive `type: "interaction"`; the old interaction category CodeableConcept belongs under `interaction.type`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The old resource identity maps to a required discriminator value on the consolidated R6 resource.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Changing only `resourceType` is insufficient: R6 validation also requires the root `type` code and enforces `cud-5` for the interaction branch. Name-based mappers can easily confuse R4 `MedicinalProductInteraction.type` with R6 root `ClinicalUseDefinition.type`.

justification.inferredGoal: Support several clinical-use issue types in one resource while keeping branch content exclusive.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Make the root discriminator optional when exactly one branch is present, or retain a legacy resource where interaction type is implied.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Once several clinical-use issue types are merged into one base resource, an explicit required `ClinicalUseDefinition.type` and invariants tying branch content to that type are a reasonable way to keep instances unambiguous. The added field is a real migration trap because R4 already had a different `type` element, but the R6 goal of computable branch discrimination is itself sound.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have made `ClinicalUseDefinition.type` `0..1` and inferred `interaction` from the presence of `ClinicalUseDefinition.interaction`, while requiring consistency when the discriminator is supplied. That would preserve transformed legacy interactions missing the new root code, but only partially meets the R6 goal: generalized processors would no longer have a uniform required classifier, branchless instances would be harder to interpret, and profile or conversion rules would still be needed for reliable migration.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Reduces migrated-instance failures but weakens uniform classification and creates validation ambiguity for branchless or inconsistent instances.

evidence.detail: R6 `type` is `1..1 code` with required binding.
The required code system includes `interaction` as the discriminator code.
The `interaction` backbone can only be used when root `type` is `interaction`.
R4 `type` was a CodeableConcept describing the interaction kind.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 `type` CodeableConcept must not be copied into the R6 root `type` primitive.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds a mandatory root discriminator because interactions are now one branch of a shared resource. This is a direct validation break and a mapping trap because both versions have an element named `type` with different meanings and datatypes.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A transformed instance missing root `type` is R6-invalid. R6-to-R4 conversion must first check `type = "interaction"`; otherwise the instance is not a medicinal-product interaction.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Always set root `ClinicalUseDefinition.type` to `interaction` for migrated R4 records, and map old `MedicinalProductInteraction.type` to `ClinicalUseDefinition.interaction.type`. Test wrong-discriminator and missing-discriminator cases.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The required discriminator is reasonable in the merged model. The backward-compatible alternative would have been a legacy profile or separate resource where the discriminator was implicit.

findings.title: Subject is now mandatory and represented as CodeableReference with changed targets

oldState.summary: R4 `subject` was optional (`0..*`) Reference to MedicinalProduct, Medication, or Substance.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 allowed an interaction record with no subject and used a plain Reference when subject was present.

newState.summary: R6 `subject` is required (`1..*`) CodeableReference to a broader/different target set including MedicinalProductDefinition and SubstanceDefinition.
newState.narrativeMd: The old `MedicinalProduct` and `Substance` targets are replaced by R6 definition resources; R6 also permits coded subjects.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Both elements identify the product, medication, substance, or other subject for which the interaction/clinical-use issue is described.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 records that omitted `subject` become invalid in R6. Records with R4 `MedicinalProduct` or `Substance` references require target migration. Generated code changes from repeated `Reference` to repeated `CodeableReference`, and R6 coded subjects or new target resource types cannot be represented cleanly in R4.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The subject identifies which product the interaction applies to; a missing or wrong target can attach advice to the wrong catalog item.

justification.inferredGoal: Make the clinical-use subject explicit and align with R6 definition-era resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep base `subject` optional and preserve a legacy Reference-compatible subject path while adding coded or broader R6 subject support.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Making the subject explicit is reasonable for a generalized clinical-use resource because the subject identifies what product, substance, device, or other item the interaction applies to. Aligning targets with the R6 definition resources is also consistent with the surrounding product-model restructuring. The breakage is substantial, but full backward compatibility would require more than a simple optional field tweak.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have kept `subject` at `0..*`, retained a Reference-compatible legacy subject representation, and added CodeableReference or additional targets separately. That would preserve some R4 records, especially those with missing subjects or Medication references, but it is incomplete and costly: old `MedicinalProduct` and `Substance` targets depend on resource families that are themselves replaced, and parallel subject forms can disagree or make validation ambiguous. Extensions or profiles are useful mitigations but are not a base-design substitute.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves sparse and legacy-reference records only by tolerating subjectless issues, obsolete targets, or duplicate subject representations.

evidence.detail: R4 `subject` is `0..*` Reference to MedicinalProduct, Medication, or Substance.
R6 `subject` is `1..*` CodeableReference with broader/different target profiles.

oldValidNewInvalidJson.description: Interaction noted without an explicit subject.

examples.examplesMd: Medication references remain the easiest case; R4 MedicinalProduct and Substance references need broader resource-family migration.

findings.narrativeMd: The subject element changed in cardinality, datatype wrapper, and target list. This is a major migration hotspot because subject is central to the clinical meaning of the interaction.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Omitted subjects are old-valid/new-invalid. Legacy product/substance references need conversion before strict R6 target validation. R6 coded subjects and new targets such as Device or NutritionProduct have no direct R4 base representation.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Audit for missing subjects. Map `Medication` directly where appropriate; map `MedicinalProduct` to `MedicinalProductDefinition` and `Substance` to `SubstanceDefinition` using separate resource-family migration rules. Define a downgrade policy for `CodeableReference.concept`.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The stricter cardinality could have been a profile or best-practice invariant, but R6 makes it a base requirement to avoid subjectless clinical-use issues.

findings.title: R4 free-text description has no direct R6 interaction field

oldState.summary: R4 had optional `description` (`0..1 string`) for the interaction described.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 provided a simple structured free-text description field.

newState.narrativeMd: The R6 branch has interactant, type, effect, incidence, management, and severity, but no general free-text description element.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: No R6 interaction child has the same role as the old general description.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Raw R4 JSON containing `description` is invalid in the R6 model, and a transform has no base destination element. Dropping the text is semantic data loss, not merely a validation adjustment.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Free-text interaction descriptions can contain clinical nuance not captured by coded fields.

justification.inferredGoal: Favor structured interaction detail in the consolidated resource.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add an optional `ClinicalUseDefinition.interaction.description` or interaction-level note element.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Favoring more structured interaction detail is reasonable, but the supplied local artifacts do not show why the R4 free-text description had to disappear from the base model. Because the element was optional and non-modifying, retaining an interaction-level text slot would have preserved legacy clinical nuance without preventing use of the R6 coded fields.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The straightforward less-breaking base design is an optional `ClinicalUseDefinition.interaction.description`, `note`, or similarly scoped text element. It would preserve most R4 `description` content as standard structured data, remain easy to ignore when unused, and avoid relying on narrative or extensions for round-trip preservation. The tradeoff is only a modest risk of overlap with generated narrative or coded interaction fields, which is a low-to-moderate long-term cost.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Low model cost; possible overlap with narrative or structured detail but little validation or interoperability burden.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `description` as `0..1 string`.
No `ClinicalUseDefinition.interaction.description` child is present.

oldValidNewInvalidJson.description: Avoid concurrent use because absorption may be reduced.

text.div: Avoid concurrent use because absorption may be reduced.

examples.examplesMd: Narrative preservation is valid FHIR but not a lossless structured field mapping.

findings.narrativeMd: The old free-text description disappears from the base R6 interaction branch. Data can be preserved in narrative or extension, but not as an equivalent standard element.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: A direct R4 property copy is R6-invalid. R6 lacks the source element for normal downgrade, so the risk is mainly forward data loss unless a migration extension or narrative convention is defined.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory records using `description`. Preserve clinically meaningful text in an agreed extension or narrative, and test that decision-support displays still include it.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: This break appears avoidable because retaining an optional text field would not weaken R6 structured fields.

findings.title: Interactant item moved under the interaction branch and its reference targets changed

oldState.summary: R4 interactant item was `1..1` Reference to MedicinalProduct, Medication, Substance, ObservationDefinition, or CodeableConcept.
oldState.narrativeMd: Each R4 interactant required exactly one coded or referenced item.

newState.summary: R6 keeps `1..1` and the CodeableConcept option, but nests the element and replaces/adds reference targets.
newState.narrativeMd: R4 `MedicinalProduct` and `Substance` references need conversion to R6 definition resources; R6 adds NutritionProduct and BiologicallyDerivedProduct targets.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The short/definition text and role match closely: this is the specific item that interacts.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The value must be moved to a new path, and legacy target references to `MedicinalProduct` or `Substance` are not in the R6 target list. R6 interactants using NutritionProduct or BiologicallyDerivedProduct cannot be represented directly in R4.

justification.inferredGoal: Align interactants with R6 product-definition resources and broaden supported interactant kinds.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep a deprecated root-level interactant alias and temporarily allow legacy product/substance targets in the base model.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Moving interactants under the interaction branch and aligning targets with `MedicinalProductDefinition` and `SubstanceDefinition` are consistent with the R6 consolidation and product-definition cleanup. The old CodeableConcept, Medication, and ObservationDefinition cases remain conceptually mappable, but old product and substance references are tied to resource families no longer present in the same form.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have retained a deprecated root-level `interactant` alias on the replacement resource and accepted old `MedicinalProduct` and `Substance` target profiles during transition. That would preserve more R4-shaped data, but only partially: it creates two same-resource paths for the same interactant fact, risks inconsistent duplicate content, and requires retaining or recognizing obsolete target resources. Official maps would reduce migration risk, but maps alone are conversion tooling rather than a backward-compatible base design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves common legacy shapes but duplicates paths and depends on supporting obsolete target resources.

evidence.detail: R4 target profiles are MedicinalProduct, Medication, Substance, and ObservationDefinition, plus CodeableConcept.
R6 target profiles are MedicinalProductDefinition, Medication, SubstanceDefinition, NutritionProduct, BiologicallyDerivedProduct, and ObservationDefinition, plus CodeableConcept.

examples.examplesMd: Choice property names remain `itemReference`/`itemCodeableConcept`, but the containing path and valid target profiles changed.

findings.narrativeMd: The interactant item is recognizable but not drop-in compatible. It moved under the R6 interaction branch and the resource targets changed.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Medication, ObservationDefinition, and CodeableConcept values are relatively direct once moved. Old MedicinalProduct/Substance references require migration. New R6 targets create downgrade gaps.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Move `interactant` under `ClinicalUseDefinition.interaction`. Convert old product/substance references with the relevant resource-family maps. Preserve CodeableConcept values directly where possible.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Target changes are partly driven by replacement of related resources, but official mappings would make the break less risky.

findings.title: Interaction effect changed from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 carried the interaction effect directly as a coded concept at the resource root.

newState.narrativeMd: The effect can now be a coded concept under `effect.concept` or a reference under `effect.reference`.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The short and definition text are effectively the same, showing a representation change for the same semantic slot.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The old root CodeableConcept must be moved and wrapped under `effect.concept`; generated properties and FHIRPath expressions change. R6 `effect.reference` values have no clean R4 CodeableConcept representation.

justification.inferredGoal: Allow either coded effects or references to reusable observation definitions.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain the coded effect shape and add a separate optional reference-valued effect instead of replacing it with CodeableReference.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: `CodeableReference` is a coherent R6 pattern for allowing either a coded effect or a reference to an `ObservationDefinition`, and it avoids separate code/reference elements in new data. However, it changes the JSON shape for existing coded effects and requires generated code and FHIRPath updates.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have kept `ClinicalUseDefinition.interaction.effect` as `CodeableConcept` for legacy coded content and added a sibling reference element, or used a choice that preserved the old coded representation. This would preserve most R4 coded effects after the broader resource/branch migration, but it is only a partial alternative because parallel code and reference fields can conflict, must be reconciled by validators and business logic, and may remain indefinitely as another duplicate representation.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves coded-data compatibility but creates parallel fields for one fact that can disagree or persist indefinitely.

evidence.detail: R4 `effect` is `0..1 CodeableConcept`.
R6 `interaction.effect` is `0..1 CodeableReference` targeting ObservationDefinition.

examples.examplesMd: R4 coded effects can usually be wrapped in `CodeableReference.concept`; R6 references need custom downgrade handling.

findings.narrativeMd: The effect field retains its broad meaning but changes representation from CodeableConcept to CodeableReference and moves under the interaction branch.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Raw R4 `effect` is invalid at the R6 path and must be wrapped. R6 reference-valued effects cannot be represented in R4 without dereferencing, extension, or loss.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map `MedicinalProductInteraction.effect` to `ClinicalUseDefinition.interaction.effect.concept`. Update generated-code assumptions and FHIRPath to handle both concept and reference.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 pattern is expressive, but a separate optional reference would have preserved direct compatibility.

findings.title: Management actions are repeatable in R6, creating downgrade loss risk

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 could carry at most one management action.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 can represent multiple management actions for the same interaction.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The element short text is the same: actions for managing the interaction.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A single R4 value maps cleanly to a one-item R6 array, so this is not a forward validation break. Valid R6 records with multiple management actions do not fit into the R4 scalar element without loss or extension.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Dropping a secondary management action could remove important mitigation advice.

justification.inferredGoal: Permit multiple management actions for a single interaction.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable because increasing `management` maximum cardinality from `1` to `*` preserves R4 single values in R6.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Allowing multiple management actions is clinically plausible and does not invalidate R4 instances: an old `0..1` value can be represented as a one-item R6 list. The compatibility concern is only reverse conversion when new R6 data uses more than one action.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base design is needed for this finding. Keeping `0..1` would improve R6-to-R4 round-tripping but would also block the R6 goal of representing multiple management actions. Extensions or concatenation could support downgrade, but those are mitigation strategies for older versions rather than alternatives to the additive R6 base design.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The tradeoff is an R6-to-R4 downgrade policy for multiple actions, not an R4-to-R6 base compatibility problem.

evidence.detail: R4 `management` is `0..1 CodeableConcept`.
R6 `interaction.management` is `0..* CodeableConcept`.

examples.examplesMd: The downgrade issue appears only when R6 uses more than one management value.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 widens management from a single value to a list. This is a notable round-trip and downgrade risk rather than an R4-to-R6 break.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 single values remain representable in R6. R6 multiple values require rejection, prioritization, text merging, or extension when converting to R4.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Wrap the R4 scalar as one R6 management item. For downgrade, define a deterministic multiple-value policy and test clinical display behavior.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The widening is a justified expressive improvement; the incompatibility is inherent to the old scalar model.

findings.title: R6 adds interaction context fields absent from R4, including modifier status, route, severity, population, and library

oldState.summary: R4 had no base elements for current/retired status, interactant route, severity, population applicability, or logic library.
oldState.narrativeMd: Comparable information in R4 would have required extensions, narrative, or related artifacts.

newState.summary: R6 adds optional `status` (modifier), route, severity, population, library, identifier, and category context.
newState.narrativeMd: `ClinicalUseDefinition.status` is the most safety-sensitive addition because modifier status changes whether interaction knowledge is current. Route, severity, population, and library add context that R4 cannot carry in base elements.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: These are local R6 elements relevant to interaction use cases with no R4 base-element counterparts.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The optional additions do not invalidate migrated R4 data, but valid R6 interaction records using them are not cleanly representable in R4. Ignoring modifier `status` can make retired or non-current interaction knowledge appear active.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Severity, route, population, and current/retired status can directly affect clinical interpretation and alerting behavior.

justification.inferredGoal: Make clinical-use knowledge more contextual and current-state aware.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Not applicable because these are optional R6 context additions that do not invalidate R4 instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Adding optional status, severity, route, population, library, identifier, and category context improves expressiveness without making R4-origin instances invalid. Marking `status` as a modifier is appropriate because current versus retired knowledge changes interpretation.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Because this finding is additive optional R6 content, backward-compatible alternative availability is not applicable under the calibration rules. R4-to-R6 migration can omit these elements. When converting R6 data back to R4, extensions, narrative, or rejection policies may be needed, but those are downgrade mitigations rather than less-breaking base R6 designs.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: They create R6-to-R4 downgrade and extension needs, but no less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is required.

evidence.detail: R6 `status` is optional, summary, and `isModifier=true`.
R6 adds interactant route.
R6 adds interaction severity.
R6 adds population references to Group.
R6 adds canonical Library references.

examples.examplesMd: A downgrade must preserve this context in extensions or narrative; otherwise consumers may miss applicability or current-state information.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds useful context fields that R4 did not have. They are not forward breaks for old instances, but they create valid R6 content that cannot be safely downgraded to R4 base elements.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4-to-R6 migration may omit these optional fields. R6-to-R4 conversion is lossy unless extension conventions are used. R6 consumers must treat `status` as a modifier.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define extension mappings for status, route, severity, population, and library before downgrading. Alerting and clinical decision support code should not ignore modifier status.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The added fields are justified enhancements. Backward compatibility can be addressed through extensions for older versions, but not by direct R4 base fields.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: No same-name R6 StructureDefinition exists. `ClinicalUseDefinition` is the likely merged counterpart, supported by the interaction backbone, interaction search parameter, and `fhir-old-types` listing.
The material removal of R4 `description` and R6 additions are reported. Other branch element moves are covered in findings.
`subject` minimum increased and `management` maximum widened. `interactant` remains `0..*`, and `interactant.item[x]` remains `1..1` after nesting.
Material datatype changes are reported for `subject` and `effect`. `interaction.type`, `incidence`, and `management` remain CodeableConcept.
Subject and interactant reference-target changes are reported. Medication and ObservationDefinition remain recognizable where applicable.
The required root `ClinicalUseDefinition.type` binding is reported. New interaction-field bindings are example strength and not base validation breaks.
R6 `cud-*` invariants are reported where they gate interaction use. Inherited `dom-*` invariants are out of scope.
No fixed, pattern, or default values were found on the mapped local fields.
No maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue changes were found on local interaction fields.
The new local R6 modifier `status` is reported. Inherited modifier fields are out of scope.
Mapped interaction fields generally remain summary where observed; inherited summary flag changes are out of scope.
No material local slicing change was found.
Semantics mostly carry over for type, effect, incidence, management, and interactant; the description removal and broader subject semantics are reported.
Major serialization changes are resourceType change, branch nesting, required discriminator, CodeableReference wrappers, and scalar-to-array management.
R6-to-R4 gaps are reported for non-interaction ClinicalUseDefinition types, CodeableReference subjects/effects, new targets, repeated management, and added context fields.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds example terminology bindings to several interaction fields
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: These bindings are `example`, so base validation does not reject codes outside the referenced value sets.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Terminology-aware applications may still want normalization, especially for SNOMED-backed value sets.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Single R4 management action can be preserved in R6
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The R6 cardinality widening allows an R4 single value to map as one list item.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: The same change is still a downgrade risk when R6 uses multiple values.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: The R6 replacement resource is active while R4 MedicinalProductInteraction was draft
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Artifact status/maturity is not an instance-level validation break.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: This does not reduce the need to handle resource identity and structural changes.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: This report uses `ClinicalUseDefinition` as the likely merged counterpart only for the R4 interaction resource. A full report should assess all clinical-use branches.
R4 `MedicinalProduct` references in `subject` and `interactant.item[x]` need migration to R6 product-definition resources.
R4 `Substance` references are replaced by `SubstanceDefinition` targets in R6 and need separate mapping guidance.
Inherited base changes are intentionally excluded from this local report.
R6 adds example bindings backed partly by SNOMED filters. Expansion comparison would improve semantic confidence.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No official R4→R6 diff, ConceptMap, or StructureMap for `MedicinalProductInteraction` to `ClinicalUseDefinition` was available locally. Replacement identity and field mapping are inferred from computable artifacts.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Official HL7 migration maps or release notes for the medicinal-product clinical-use resource consolidation.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Narrative specification pages were not consulted, so rationale and intended migration semantics may be incomplete.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review R5/R6 narrative pages and change notes for `ClinicalUseDefinition` and retired medicinal-product resources.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology comparison did not expand SNOMED-based R6 value sets, so terminology impact is limited to binding strength and value set identity rather than code-level deltas.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run terminology expansion against the R6 value sets with version-pinned code systems.
